lastCompletedStory.title: Make RunTriageOptions.clock optional, mirroring the unused-clock command pattern

nextStoryContext: US-002 made RunTriageOptions.clock optional (clock?: ClockFn) in src/commands/triage.ts, rewrote its doc comment to drop the 'required/reserved-for-future' claim, removed the dead 'clock: () => new Date().toISOString()' injection at the dispatchTriage call site in index.ts (the only remaining occurrence of that literal in index.ts now belongs to a different, unrelated dispatcher at ~line 1536 and was NOT touched), and deleted all 16 dead 'clock: () => ...' call-site lines from test/triage.test.ts (more than the '~8' the PRD note estimated; verified exhaustively via grep, not by sampling). Left test/integration/triage-real-git.test.ts and test/integration/triage-ref-only.test.ts untouched -- they still pass a clock literal, which remains valid TypeScript now that the field is optional, and the story's AC only named test/triage.test.ts. Next story (US-003) refactors runKahn (src/issues/rank.ts, per the PRD description mentioning 'the CAM-108 review') under the cognitive-complexity budget and drops the rank.ts biome noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity override/suppression -- read src/issues/rank.ts and biome.json (or wherever the per-file override lives) in full before editing; this is a pure refactor (extract-helper style, same family as the noExcessiveLinesPerFunction extractions already documented in patterns.md) with no external library surface, so Step 5.5 will again likely be 'no_external_lib_touched' unless runKahn touches something unexpected.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure internal TypeScript interface change (clock field optionality) plus dead call-site removal; no external library API surface touched.
